gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a stylus costs per hour of play. For its own top pick, the AT-LP70XBT, the stock AT-VMN95C stylus costs $32 at Turntable Lab and Audio-Technica says to replace it after 300 hours, which works out to about 10.7¢ an hour or about 7¢ per 40-minute album.
standout_why: turntableverse.com, opened 2026-11-13, names the LP70XBT's AT-VMN95C stylus but gives no stylus life, no stylus price and no cost per hour or per record. The two pages ChatGPT cited, whathifi.com and loudersound.com, could not be read: WebFetch got back only the title and 137 characters, so I could not check them. vinylpickup.com failed with a TLS error. None of the rival text I could read pairs a stylus price with a rated life.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's choice of the LP70XBT on running cost. Its stock stylus is the cheapest of the candidates ($32, against $36 for the ATN3600LC that the LP60XBT, the JBL Spinner BT and, per Turntable Lab, the Sony PS-LX3BT use). It also has the only upgrade path within the same stylus family: the $52 elliptical VMN95E and the $109 nude VMN95EN clip into the same cartridge. The 300-hour figure was opened only for the LP70X, so a per-hour comparison across all candidates is not possible yet. The difference is in stylus price and upgrade options, not proven stylus life.
